headline: Medium prompt-injection and data-leakage risk from shared editor/repo context; no direct evidence of severe cross-agent conflict.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Copilot reads repo context and open editor buffers, while Superset consumes the Superset API and can act on analytics content. A shared workspace or copied output could let attacker-controlled code/comments in Copilot’s context influence Superset’s downstream interpretation. The profiles do not show a direct shared channel, so this is not high.
conditions: IF Copilot output is copied into Superset prompts or dashboards without review, injection becomes plausible.
IF both agents operate on the same repository or workspace content, attacker-controlled text can bridge them.
mitigations: Review Copilot-generated text before pasting into Superset.
Keep Copilot and Superset on separate workspaces for the same task.
Strip instructions from copied code/comments before reuse.
Use a human verification step for any Copilot-derived narrative.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between editor output and analytics inputs.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Copilot touches source code and open editor buffers and sends requests to api.githubcopilot.com, while Superset has allowlisted network egress and no declared sensitive data classes. The profiles do not show a shared filesystem or PHI/secret handling, so leakage is limited to ordinary workspace content and is not clearly severe.
conditions: IF the same sensitive files are opened in Copilot and then exposed through Superset inputs, leakage risk increases.
IF Superset is configured to ingest copied code or notes from Copilot, those contents may leave the local workflow.
mitigations: Avoid opening secrets in Copilot sessions.
Do not paste repo snippets into Superset unless necessary.
Use separate accounts and workspaces.
Redact sensitive fields before transfer.
requires-engineering: enforce data-loss-prevention filters on copied content.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Copilot can write the filesystem and modify git state, while Superset only advertises allowlisted egress and a Superset API surface. There is no evidence that both write the same mutable resource or share locks, so direct conflict is possible only if an operator connects them to the same repo or dataset.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same git working tree, write conflicts can occur.
IF Superset is used to mutate a shared dataset while Copilot edits the repo, concurrent changes may collide.
mitigations: Assign one agent per mutable resource.
Pause one agent before the other writes.
Commit Copilot changes before Superset-driven updates.
Use branch-based workflows.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared datasets or repos.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Copilot can generate code and edits, and Superset can consume API-driven analytics content. If Superset treats Copilot-produced text or code as authoritative without verification, errors can cascade into incorrect dashboards or actions. The profiles do not show automated action-taking, so this stays medium rather than high.
conditions: IF Superset ingests Copilot-generated SQL, metrics, or narratives without validation, downstream errors can propagate.
IF Copilot edits are accepted into a pipeline that Superset later renders, the same mistake can be amplified.
mitigations: Require validation of Copilot output before ingestion.
Compare Copilot-generated SQL against known-good queries.
Use staging dashboards for review.
Add checksum or review gates before publishing.
requires-engineering: implement automated semantic validation of generated artifacts.

E_compliance.rationale: Copilot is a closed-source GitHub/Microsoft service that handles repo context, while Superset is open-source and shows no declared sensitive data classes or residency constraints. No explicit residency or certification mismatch is documented, so compliance risk is limited to policy gaps if sensitive code is routed into Copilot.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into Copilot prompts, organizational policy may be implicated.
IF Superset is configured with sensitive datasets and Copilot is used on the same material, residency or retention review may be needed.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Copilot prompts.
Document which datasets Superset may access.
Review vendor retention settings.
Separate regulated and non-regulated workflows.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for regulated data routing.
